entries.name: Variable holds several values at once
entries.description: Believes a variable keeps a history of the values assigned to it, or that assigning a new value adds to the old one, instead of replacing it.
indicators: Trace answers list every value a variable was given
Chooses the first or a combined value after several assignments

causes: Everyday meaning of "store" as a container that accumulates
strategies: Use the labelled-box model: a new value replaces what is in the box
Trace tables with one column per variable, crossing out old values
Predict-then-run with the pseudocode editor
entries.student_tip: A variable holds one value at a time. When you assign a new value, the old one is replaced.

entries.name: Assignment works in both directions

strategies: Read ← aloud as "becomes" or "gets"

entries.student_tip: In X ← Y, only X changes. Read the arrow as "X becomes the value of Y".

Code output where a comparison is mistaken for assignment

entries.student_tip: A primary key must be different for every record and never empty. Names can repeat, so they are poor keys.
entries.evidence: At least two opportunities; a distractor linked to this misconception chosen on two or more different questions, or three or more errors across at least two related questions.

entries.name: Field, record and table confused
entries.description: Calls a row a field or a column a record.
indicators: Answers "record" for a column heading
question_patterns: Count fields and records in a table
causes: Terms learned without the table picture
strategies: Label a printed table: columns are fields, rows are records
entries.student_tip: Fields are columns (one kind of data); records are rows (everything about one item).
entries.evidence: At least two opportunities; a distractor linked to this misconception chosen on two or more different questions, or three or more errors across at least two related questions.

entries.name: SQL clause roles
entries.description: Puts conditions in SELECT, confuses WHERE with ORDER BY, or believes COUNT adds values while SUM counts rows.
indicators: Uses ORDER BY to filter
Swaps SUM and COUNT
question_patterns: Predict the output of a query
strategies: Build queries clause by clause and run them in DBWOW
entries.student_tip: SELECT chooses columns, FROM chooses the table, WHERE chooses rows, ORDER BY sorts them. COUNT counts rows; SUM adds values.
entries.evidence: At least two opportunities; a distractor linked to this misconception chosen on two or more different questions, or three or more errors across at least two related questions.
